sections.markdown:
## C2 — Trailer hookup, loading, driving and checklist continuation facts, then confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: ABS versus standard brakes in a winter skid, night following time, work zone planning and getting traction
Continuation facts for trailer towing and winter traction plus confusable pairs among headlight, following-time, braking and trailer rules; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A02
Night driving alone calls for at least one added second of following time, while unfamiliar roads at night call for at least two. [A02]
Why it matters: group night driving; confusable familiar versus unfamiliar roads.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A04
Expect work zone delays and plan for them by leaving earlier, and use alternate routes to avoid work zones when you can. [A04]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0128]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A06
Check that the defroster works by turning on the fan and placing your hand on the dashboard. [A06]
Why it matters: group winter driving; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A08
To get traction when stuck, pour sand, cat litter, gravel or salt in the wheels' path, or try cardboard, newspaper or brush under the wheels. [A08]
Why it matters: group winter driving; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A08
In a winter skid with ABS, do not pump the brakes but hold steady pressure and expect the pedal to pulse, while with standard brakes you pump them gently. [A08]
Why it matters: group winter driving; confusable ABS versus standard brakes.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A08
If at all possible, do not abandon your vehicle in the roadway. [A08]
Why it matters: group winter driving; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A08
The manual notes that trailers are towed billions of miles every year, making towing a common everyday activity even if any one person does it only now and then. [A08]
Why it matters: group trailers; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A09
Your judgment and common sense are key to safe trailering, and driver error contributes to the large majority of crashes involving vehicle-trailer combinations. [A09]
Why it matters: group trailers; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A09
Learn the correct hookup for your vehicle and trailer: couple the trailer to the hitch ball, hook up the safety chains and plug in the trailer lights, and finish the whole process without stopping to do something else. [A09]
Why it matters: group trailer hookup; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A09
Before leaving, check that the coupler and hitch ball are properly connected, and make sure both side mirrors are clean and undamaged. [A09]
Why it matters: group trailer hookup; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A11
After a sway, check that the cargo is heavier in front and reload if needed, keeping heavy items on the trailer floor rather than stacked on other items. [A11]
Why it matters: group trailer loading; difficulty medium.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A11
Pack cargo tightly, secure partial loads with tie-downs or straps and packing material, and never exceed the trailer maker's maximum gross weight. [A11]
Why it matters: group trailer loading; difficulty low.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A11
Towing calls for adjusting your driving to the vehicle, accepting a slower pace, which also saves fuel and lowers the chance of losing control. [A11]
Why it matters: group trailer driving; difficulty low.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A11
Slow down before you start down a grade with a trailer, not after. [A11]
Why it matters: group trailer driving; confusable before versus after the downgrade.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A11
A vehicle with a trailer needs more distance to stop and more time and distance to pass, so leave extra space ahead, and even more in rain, snow or fog. [A11]
Why it matters: group trailer driving; difficulty medium.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0135]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A12
With a trailer, never pass on hills or curves, and remember the trailer does not follow directly behind the car, so turns need extra room. [A12]
Why it matters: group trailer driving; difficulty medium.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec15-R17 | anchor: A12
If you are unsure how to hook up, load or drive with a trailer, get advice from a trailer professional. [A12]
Why it matters: group trailer tips; difficulty low.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec15-R18 | anchor: A12
Before driving and at every fuel stop, walk around the rig and recheck the hitch and coupler tightness, safety chains, lights and tire pressures. [A12]
Why it matters: group trailer tips; difficulty medium.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec15-R19 | anchor: A12
If you hear an unusual noise or suspect trouble while towing, stop at a safe place off the road to check it. [A12]
Why it matters: group trailer tips; difficulty low.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0136]

FACT_ID: sec15-R20 | anchor: A13
On long trips, plan rest stops instead of driving straight through, so you drive in daylight while rested and alert. [A13]
Why it matters: group trailer tips; difficulty low.
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0137]

FACT_ID: sec15-R21 | anchor: A13
The safe trailering checklist covers a front-heavy load, a tight hitch, attached chains, working lights, correct tire pressures, reduced speed, thinking ahead, frequent rest, frequent inspection, a secure load and wearing your seat belt. [A13]
Why it matters: group trailer tips; difficulty medium.
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0137]
